Alicia — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're open to a compromise that preserves predictability for both sides. Copying Jordan (AE) and Neha (legal) so we can turn around a marked‑up counter.

High level proposal: 
- Auto‑renew opt‑out: move to 60 days for standard customers but offer Pulse a one‑time 90‑day opt‑out in Year 1 as a commercial concession.
- TfC: Redwood can accept a Termination for Convenience right limited to Year 1 only, with 60 days' notice and a prorated credit for unused pre‑paid fees equal to 30 days of run‑rate (we can discuss exact calculation). For pilot accounts < $50k TCV we can shorten the wind‑down to 14 days.

Neha — please prepare a counter redline reflecting the above options (we want language options, not a single take‑it‑or‑leave‑it clause). Jordan — I'll need you to confirm whether one‑time 90‑day opt‑out materially impacts forecast/commitments for Q3.

Alicia — if that sounds workable I'll send the redline and we can loop in procurement. Goal: keep you on track for 6/28.

Internal note — forwarding Pulse's redline. Neha, below are the two discrete asks we need alternative language for so we can present options to the customer: 

1) Auto‑renew opt‑out window: customer wants 90d. We prefer 60d. Suggest we give a one‑time 90d opt‑out in Year 1 only; thereafter 60d standard. 
   - Option A (Commercial concession): "Customer may elect a one‑time 90‑day opt‑out prior to the first renewal. All subsequent renewals require 60 days' notice."
   - Option B (Contractual): "Renewals shall occur automatically for successive 12‑month periods unless either party provides written notice at least 60 days prior to the end of the then‑current term. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for the initial renewal only Customer may provide notice at least 90 days prior."

2) Termination for Convenience: customer wants 90d + 30d prorated credit. We prefer tighter notice and explicit financial balancing. 
   - Option 1 (Balanced): "Either party may terminate for convenience upon 60 days' prior written notice; Customer shall receive a refund of pre‑paid fees for the portion of the term remaining after the effective date of termination, calculated on a pro rata basis; in addition Redwood will provide a transition credit equal to 30 days of average monthly billing for the prior 3 months for agreements > $50k TCV. Pilot accounts (TCV < $50k) receive a 14‑day credit."
   - Option 2 (Conservative): "TfC allowed with 60 days' notice; refund only pro rata, no transition credit. Customer may negotiate a limited pilot carveout in a signed SOW."

Please draft redlines for both items and attach Redwood_Counter_TfC_v1.docx. Include a short rationale paragraph we can send with the redline to procurement.

—Michael

Alicia — thanks for the patience while we reviewed. Attached is a concise counter that presents two clear options for each of your asks so procurement can choose the path that works best for stakeholders. Summary here so procurement can triage quickly: 

Auto‑renew (quick summary):
- Option A (preferred for Redwood): Standard 12‑month term with 60‑day opt‑out on renewals; Pulse may exercise a one‑time 90‑day opt‑out prior to the first renewal.
- Option B: Contract language granting the initial 90‑day opt‑out explicitly (same commercial effect, slightly different drafting).

Termination for Convenience (quick summary):
- Option 1 (balanced): 60 days' notice; pro rata refund; transition credit equal to 30 days of average monthly billing for agreements with TCV > $50k; pilot carveout (TCV < $50k) gets 14‑day transition credit.
- Option 2 (conservative): 60 days' notice; pro rata refund only; pilot carveouts handled by SOW.

Why this approach: it protects Redwood's capacity planning and revenue predictability while giving Pulse a measured runway to wind down if needed. The one‑time 90‑day opt‑out is intended as a commercial concession to get you comfortable without making future renewals unstable.

Next steps: I've attached the redline (Redwood_Counter_TfC_v1.docx). If Pulse prefers Option 1 for TfC and the one‑time 90‑day opt‑out we'll route a short amendment and can start a DocuSign flow.
